record.paper_title: Pulsars and Millisecond Pulsars I: Advancements, Open Questions and finding Gaps via statistical insights
record.original_question: How do different binary-system configurations affect the spin-up of neutron stars into pulsars or millisecond pulsars? In particular, how do structural properties of the neutron star, such as its spin and magnetic field, together with orbital parameters such as semi-major axis and eccentricity, change the efficiency and outcome of the accretion-driven transfer of angular momentum that accelerates the neutron star's rotation?

evidence.quote: 2. Binary Interactions: How do various binary configurations—such as structural properties (e.g., spin and magnetic field of neutron stars) and orbital parameters (e.g., semi-major axis and eccentricity)—influence the spin-up processes of neutron stars

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a binary system consisting of a neutron star of mass $M_{\mathrm{NS}}$, radius $R_{\mathrm{NS}}$, moment of inertia $I$, surface dipolar magnetic field strength $B$, and initial spin angular frequency $\Omega_0$, in orbit with a companion star of mass $M_c$ on a Keplerian orbit characterized by semi-major axis $a$ and eccentricity $e$. Suppose mass transfer occurs via either Roche-lobe overflow or stellar-wind accretion at a rate $\dot{M}(t)$, and that accreted matter forms (where applicable) a Keplerian disk truncated at the magnetospheric (Alfvén) radius
$$r_m \;=\; \left(\frac{B^2 R_{\mathrm{NS}}^6}{\dot{M}\sqrt{2 G M_{\mathrm{NS}}}}\right)^{2/7},$$
with corotation radius $r_{\mathrm{co}} = (G M_{\mathrm{NS}}/\Omega^2)^{1/3}$. The angular momentum evolution of the neutron star is governed by
$$I\,\dot{\Omega} \;=\; \dot{M}\,\sqrt{G M_{\mathrm{NS}} r_m}\;-\;N_{\mathrm{mag}}(\Omega,B,r_m,r_{\mathrm{co}}),$$
where $N_{\mathrm{mag}}$ is the magnetic propeller/braking torque, which depends on the fastness parameter $\omega_s = (r_m/r_{\mathrm{co}})^{3/2}$.

Determine, as a function of the parameters $(B, \Omega_0, a, e, M_c, \dot{M})$:
(i) the conditions under which the neutron star is spun up to the millisecond regime (final spin period $P_{\mathrm{spin}} \lesssim 10$ ms);
(ii) the total accreted mass $\Delta M$ and timescale $\tau_{\mathrm{rec}}$ required for recycling to that regime;
(iii) the dependence of the spin-up efficiency $\eta = \Delta\Omega/\Delta M$ on orbital eccentricity $e$ and semi-major axis $a$, including the role of periastron-enhanced accretion in eccentric orbits;
(iv) the threshold magnetic field above which the propeller effect prevents spin-up entirely.

Provide quantitative criteria and asymptotic regimes characterizing the outcome (isolated recycled pulsar versus millisecond pulsar versus spin-down) in terms of the listed parameters.
artifact.status_search_result: The recycling scenario for millisecond pulsar formation is broadly accepted, but the detailed dependence of spin-up efficiency on binary structural and orbital parameters (especially eccentricity, magnetic-field decay during accretion, and the propeller/accretion transition) remains an active area of research with no closed-form quantitative solution; this is generally treated as an open modeling problem in pulsar astrophysics.

status_evidence.title: Recycled pulsars and the millisecond pulsar formation channel
status_evidence.snippet: The standard recycling scenario explains MSP formation via accretion-induced spin-up in low-mass X-ray binaries, but quantitative details remain debated.
status_evidence.claim: The general recycling picture is accepted while quantitative parameter dependences remain open.

status_evidence.title: Accretion torques and propeller effect in neutron-star binaries
status_evidence.snippet: The transition between accretor and propeller regimes and the resulting spin evolution depend sensitively on magnetic field, mass-transfer rate, and orbital configuration.
status_evidence.claim: Spin-up efficiency depends on B, dot M, and orbital parameters in ways that are still being modeled.
